prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: automated hospital medication dispensing/returns; goals timeliness, pharmacist oversight, traceability. Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Elements: Medication Order Gateway validates patient/product/dose/route/timing, rejects incomplete updates with reason, routes to pharmacy review, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot uses Snapshot to compare requested qty vs dispense events/cabinet balances; checks order active/authorization valid; excludes cancelled orders; stops pick on exception, holds package; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag (used by North Ward Cabinet Controller). Pharmacy Verification Station does final check, blocks mismatch, produces Batch Release Note. Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temps, reports excursions/connectivity loss. East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles route via Pneumatic Tube Network (admits only reconciled loads); East sends Tube Route Exception Ticket. North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers record arrivals, block when Out of Service. Medication Return Kiosk produces Return Bin Audit Label (used by Pharmacy Technician). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist approves/rejects corrections, produces Dose Exception Review Slip, seeks higher-level decision if inconclusive (hold stays). Pharmacy Technician gathers evidence, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card, confirms no unresolved discrepancy before routine replenishment. Medication Safety Officer reviews diversion/repeated high-risk/harm events, sends Diversion Review Packet to IT Operations Specialist, who checks logs without changing disposition and records software/connectivity findings. Biomedical Engineer evaluates mechanical/sensor faults, advises return to service. Registered Nurse verifies loads, never bypasses. Charge Nurse sends Cabinet Downtime Notice. Hospital Courier produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. Rules: serious exceptions escalated immediately; final disposition records reviewer, evidence, released/corrected/withheld; reconciliation by stable order ID with timestamps/transaction IDs; corrected order supersedes old values; duplicates flagged not added; partial dispense computed conservatively; patient/medication/qty disagreement holds transaction; outcome records matched values, differences, disposition. Modes: normal routing; manual/alternate delivery; Out of Service.

New part:
S161: North Ward Cabinet Controller applies the North Ward medication access rules when evaluating a cabinet transaction.
S162: Its ward-specific configuration defines permitted medication locations, access roles, and transaction limits for each cabinet.
S163: The configuration associates each medication location with the product identifiers and quantity thresholds used by the ward.
S164: Cabinet availability is calculated from the last confirmed inventory count and subsequent recorded movements.
S165: Configured maximum and minimum quantities guide replenishment decisions without overriding an active clinical restriction.
S166: Access rules require an authenticated user role appropriate to the requested medication and transaction type.
S167: High-risk medication locations can require an additional confirmation before a removal is accepted.
S168: The controller rejects a transaction when its location mapping does not match the reconciled medication identity.
S169: Configuration changes are versioned, reviewed, and recorded with the effective time and approving authority.
S170: If the controller has not received a current approved configuration, it prevents routine dispensing and reports the condition for investigation.
S171: Bluejay maintains a time-stamped temperature history for each refrigerated medication compartment and raises an alarm when a configured limit is exceeded.
S172: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler applies approved upper and lower temperature limits to each monitored compartment.
S173: Calibrated probes report readings at configured intervals, and the cooler records probe identity and calibration status with each reading.
S174: Refrigerated stock is identified by medication, lot, and expiration date so that each unit remains traceable to its storage history.
S175: When readings exceed a limit or a probe becomes unavailable, the affected stock is marked ineligible for routine dispensing.
S176: The cooler preserves the affected stock in its current controlled environment while the condition is assessed.
S177: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler uses the handoff card to compare a transfer’s recorded custody time with its temperature history.
S178: A Clinical Pharmacist reviews excursion details and determines whether affected stock may be released, quarantined, or discarded under pharmacy policy.
S179: The cooler retains the disposition status against the affected lot and prevents stock marked ineligible from being selected for routine dispensing.
S180: Authorized access to refrigerated compartments is recorded with the user identity, access time, and affected stock identifiers.
S181: Door-open duration is monitored so that an access event that threatens temperature control can be distinguished from a brief inspection.
S182: Temperature alarms remain active during loss of network connectivity, and local records are retained until communication is restored.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
